title: Deterministic payload envelope PRD: progressive tool handoff, resume semantics, and schema rollback acceptance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: define a set of acceptance criteria and operational requirements for a deterministic "compact payload envelope" format used for progressive (streamed) structured output and function/tool handoffs. This ticket covers schema markers, resume tokens, canonical error classes, and a minimal rollback/compatibility strategy so Redwood-hosted and private deployments can safely route partial emissions to tool adapters and downstream processors. Scope explicitly excludes full wire-format changes to the runtime; this is a combinable API/contract spec that runtime and SDK teams will implement.
out_of_scope: Do not change default model tokenizer behavior, do not introduce new RPC endpoints; implementation changes will be handled in ENG tickets referenced in dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Compact payload envelope: each emitted frame (stream or non-stream) must be wrapped in a single-line JSON 'envelope' with required top-level keys: 'env_v': 1, 'seq':<integer>, 'type':<string>, 'payload':<object|string|null>, 'resume_token':<string|null>, 'commit':<boolean>, 'sig':<string|null>. - Note: the actual JSON example is in linked PRD artifact; runtime must support parsing the single-line envelope without needing reassembly of multi-line frames.

Progressive handoff semantics: a tool adapter must be able to accept a sequence of envelopes where 'seq' is strictly increasing and 'resume_token' on a later envelope can be used to request re-send of missing seq ranges via a 'replay' API (IDEMPOTENT replays only).

Resume tokens: tokens must encode a monotonic checkpoint (opaque to callers) and be stable across short schema upgrades; tokens can be invalidated by a schema-rollback marker but must produce a clear error class when used against an incompatible stream.

Streaming error modes: distinguish three canonical error classes in the envelope 'type' field: 'recoverable' (transient parsing/partial payload — allow replay or patch), 'terminal' (non-retryable, drop tool handoff and surface human-readable failure), and 'degraded' (payload emitted but with quality flags — accept but emit telemetry). Each error instance must include an RFC-like code (e.g., RINF_1001) and human message.

Partial payload repair: when an adapter receives a 'recoverable' envelope, it should call the 'replay' flow using the most recent resume_token and then apply patch envelopes where 'type' == 'patch' to mutate previously stored payloads; acceptance requires successful round-trip replay in an integration test harness.

Commit semantics: at least one envelope in the stream must set 'commit': true to indicate canonical completion of the structured object; consumers must tolerate absent 'commit' by applying an expiration policy (configurable TTL) and emitting a 'commit_timeout' telemetry event after TTL expires.

Idempotency and deduplication: a consumer must deduplicate by 'seq' + source-id for at-least-once delivery scenarios; unit tests should demonstrate duplicate envelope suppression and correct ordering under replays.

Schema evolution and rollback: introduce a versioned 'schema_hint' optional key. When a schema rollback marker is emitted (envelope with 'type' == 'schema_rollback' and 'commit' == true), consumers must treat subsequent resume_token replays as incompatible and return a well-defined error indicating 'schema_mismatch' with remediation steps.

Fallback to non-streamed contract: if the upstream indicates 'streaming_disabled' in initial metadata, the system should support returning the full object in a single envelope with commit==true and identical validation paths as the streamed sequence.

Observability: each envelope processed must produce three telemetry rows: envelope_ingest_latency_ms, envelope_apply_success:boolean, envelope_error_code:string (nullable). Dashboards must be available in Console for the structured-output-stability project within the release window.

End-to-end tests: create an automated scenario that simulates a 10-envelope progressive emission with an injected recoverable error at envelope 4, triggers a replay using resume_token, applies a patch, and completes with commit; integration must assert final payload equals expected canonical object and that telemetry contains a replay event and 'commit' marker.

Backward compatibility: older clients without 'resume_token' support must be able to consume commit-only envelopes; acceptance must include a compatibility smoke test against a curated list of older SDK versions.

Security and PII: resume_token and sig fields must not contain raw PII; tokens must be HMAC-signed using a per-deployment key. Security SME sign-off (security_review_required) is required before release.
Runtime SLO impact: projected P99 extra latency under typical payloads must be < 5ms per envelope; performance regression tests must be run and pass threshold within the release.
Documented migration guide: PRD linked guide and SDK migration notes for tool adapters and customers must be published and linked in the ticket before marking Done.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for envelope serializer/parser (edge cases: null payload, long resume_token). 2) Integration harness simulating network reorders and replays. 3) Compatibility smoke test with older SDKs. 4) Load test (10k envelopes/sec) to validate P99 envelope processing latency. 5) Security review checklist run and HMAC key rotation test.
notes:
- We are intentionally opting for a compact, single-line envelope to simplify streaming interop with existing runtime multiplexers.
- Runtime changes will be gated by ENG-21012 (serializer) and ENG-21456 (adapter replay service).
- Consider turning 'sig' into an optional compact Ed25519 signature if HSM latencies permit; design doc in Confluence.
